# Extension risk report: ExtRay Demo Cookie Manager v1.0.0

## Verdict: concerning

No high-severity harmful behavior was confirmed against source, but broad or anomalous capability with notable signals in permissions (high), obfuscation (notable) places the extension above low-risk — the user should weigh whether the access is warranted.

## Summary

This extension is a cookie manager that can view, edit, and delete cookies for any website you visit. It requests broad access to all websites and your cookies, which gives it significant control over your browsing data. The most important thing to weigh is whether you need a tool with this level of access to all your cookies across every site.

### Technical summary

The extension performs full CRUD operations on cookies across all stores (finding 7) and requests both the cookies permission and <all_urls> host access (finding 1). It includes an eval sink in a bundled jEditable library (finding 2) and standard jQuery innerHTML sinks (finding 5). Network destinations include demo-cookies.example and google.com, with three unresolved XHR destinations in bundled libraries (finding 8). A claim regarding cookie data exported to the system clipboard was checked and refuted, and a concern about DevTools panel messaging without sender validation was checked and cleared.

> Cookie manager for viewing and editing browser cookies.

## Findings

The asserted findings of this report. A "verified behavior" was adjudicated against the extension's actual source code and CONFIRMED; an "observed capability" is an API/permission/string/destination present in the evidence, with no behavioral mechanism asserted.

### 1. Cookies permission combined with <all_urls> host access — observed capability

The manifest requests both the cookies permission and <all_urls> host permissions, enabling read/write/delete access to all cookies for every site the user visits. This is flagged as a dangerous combination (cookies+broad-host) in the manifest analysis.

Confidence (as generated): high.

Evidence:
  - `manifest.json` (cites `"permissions":["tabs","cookies","contextMenus","unlimitedStorage","storage","clipboardWrite"]`)
  - `manifest.json` (cites `"host_permissions":["<all_urls>"]`)

### 2. eval sink in bundled jquery.jeditable.js library — observed capability

The jEditable library (imported by devtools/panel.js) contains an eval call that concatenates a dynamic 'string' argument into a JavaScript expression: eval("var json = " + string). If user-controlled or cookie-derived data reaches this sink through the editable table interface, it could result in code execution within the DevTools panel context.

Confidence (as generated): medium.

Evidence:
  - `lib/jquery.jeditable.js:372:20` (cites `eval ("var json = " + string)`)

### 3. Navigation to demo-cookies.example help pages — observed capability

The extension opens tabs to https://demo-cookies.example/#start and #faq via chrome.tabs.create. This domain appears to be a demo/example domain associated with the extension's purpose.

Confidence (as generated): high.

Evidence:
  - `js/background.js:121:6` (cites `chrome.tabs.create({ url: 'https://demo-cookies.example/#start' })`)
  - `options_pages/options_page_chooser.js:9:18` (cites `https://demo-cookies.example/#start`)
  - `options_pages/options_page_chooser.js:12:18` (cites `https://demo-cookies.example/#faq`)

### 4. Static google.com reference in DevTools panel — observed capability

devtools/panel.js references https://google.com as a static argument to a function named createList. This appears to be a demo/test URL for the cookie manager's display functionality, but the exact data flow is not fully resolved from the evidence.

Confidence (as generated): low.

Evidence:
  - `devtools/panel.js:41:17` (symbol `createList`, cites `https://google.com`)

### 5. jQuery innerHTML assignment sinks in bundled library — observed capability

The bundled jQuery 3.3.1 library contains multiple innerHTML assignment sinks, including one that processes HTML via htmlPrefilter. These are standard jQuery DOM manipulation patterns but represent potential XSS sinks if untrusted data is passed through jQuery's HTML parsing APIs.

Confidence (as generated): low.

Evidence:

  - `lib/jquery-3.3.1.min.js:2:49619` (cites `t.innerHTML=e`)

### 6. Context menu integration for cookie management — observed capability

The extension registers a context menu item 'ExtRay Demo Cookie Manager' for page contexts, which triggers a showPopup function when clicked. This is consistent with the extension's stated purpose of providing cookie management access.

Confidence (as generated): high.

Evidence:
  - `js/background.js:45:8` (cites `chrome.contextMenus.create({ id: 'demoCookieManagerMenu', title: 'ExtRay Demo Cookie Manager', contexts: ['page'] })`)
  - `js/background.js:71:2` (cites `chrome.contextMenus.onClicked.addListener((info, tab) => { if (info.menuItemId === 'demoCookieManagerMenu') { showPopup(info, tab); } })`)

### 7. Cookie modification and deletion across all stores — observed capability

The extension performs full CRUD operations on cookies (getAll, get, set, remove) across background, popup, devtools panel, and options pages. The user_preferences.js page iterates all cookies and re-sets them (shortenCookies), demonstrating bulk cookie modification capability across all cookie stores.

Three unresolved network destinations were identified in bundled jQuery and Uniform libraries (xhr-open and navigation.url AST roles with dynamic values). ## Excluded claims (checked, NOT findings)

Generated claims that did NOT survive verification, recorded for audit with the reason each was excluded. None of these is asserted as a behavior of this extension.

### Cookie data exported to system clipboard — REFUTED against source

The extension retrieves all cookies via chrome.cookies.getAll and formats them into cookie file formats (Netscape and semicolon-separated) in cookie_helpers.js, then uses document.execCommand('copy') in utils.js to place the formatted cookie data on the system clipboard. The destination is the user's clipboard, consistent with an export feature.

Mechanism (claimed): chrome.cookies.getAll retrieves all cookies, cookie_helpers.js formats them into Netscape/semicolon cookie file text, and js/utils.js copies the result to the clipboard via document.execCommand('copy').

Evidence (as cited):
  - `js/utils.js:52:2` (cites `chrome.cookies.getAll({}, function (cookieL) { ... }`)
  - `js/utils.js:139:2` (cites `document.execCommand('copy')`)
  - `js/cookie_helpers.js:149:14` (cites `// Semicolon separated Cookie File\n`)
  - `js/cookie_helpers.js:150:14` (cites `// This file was generated by ExtRay Demo Cookie Manager\n`)

Source verification: **refuted**. The source contains a call to chrome.cookies.getAll, but it is only used to delete matching cookies; there is no code that passes the retrieved cookies to cookie_helpers.js for formatting, nor any code that calls copyToClipboard with that data. The copyToClipboard function merely copies a supplied text string and is never invoked with cookie data.
